projects.title: Beirut Marathon Women’S Race
projects.description: We participated in the Beirut Marathon Women’s Race to support our cause. We had 315 women, men and children running for Stand for Women and contributed at helping women-owned businesses in Beirut. Participants were Individuals and 14 corporates and Initiatives; which were Holdal GAA, Arab Bank, CMACGM, L’Oreal Lebanon, Entotox, FNF, Grant Thornton, Tinol, Total energies, Vitas, Merit shipping, KFF Khalil Fattal, Bemo Bank, Cannelle and Life 4 youth. Moreover, our partners during the race were Bio Oil and Entotox.

projects.title: Wing Women Lebanon
projects.description: Our partnership with Wing Women Lebanon, Melie the founder keeps on fighting to end period poverty by producing reusable pads. She is creating job opportunities for women from vulnerable communities. The pads are all sold commercially or/and to other organizations (NGO/charities), since period poverty is affecting 76% of those menstruated in Lebanon. By this, we are providing economic empowerment to women whilst simultaneously reducing period poverty in Lebanon and being eco-friendly.

projects.title: Eres
projects.description: Thank you to the Eres, a french lingerie brand for their donation of 500 pieces of fine lingerie, sleepwear & homewear to the beneficiaries of Stand For Women and their employees, during December 2020. This was possible thanks to the relentless efforts of Accelerate Beirut led by Alia Atieh & the support of Life lebanon UK.
body: Thank you to the Eres, a french lingerie brand for their donation of 500 pieces of fine lingerie, sleepwear & homewear to the beneficiaries of Stand For Women and their employees, during December 2020. This was possible thanks to the relentless efforts of Accelerate Beirut led by Alia Atieh & the support of Life lebanon UK.

projects.title: Google
projects.description: In November 2021 we started this collaboration with Google by locating 70+ women-owned businesses on Google Maps and we identified all the businesses, monitored and followed up, ground visits, and outreach and support. Then, we had an event at BDD, a full training session offered by “Maharat min Google” for beginners and advanced level that followed with coffee and lunch break.

projects.title: Fast Forward
projects.description: In collaboration with Fast Forward 2030, and under the Flash Forward program. A financial grant combined with a basic digital marketing training delivered by Socialprise Marketing Agency, was offered to 11 women-led businesses that helped them to cover employee’s bonuses, purchase stocks and equipment and to acquire new brands. Besides, the entrepreneurs along with their employees and more than 70 women-owned SMEs attended the “Stand Up Against Street Harassment” International Training, which was held in collaboration with L’Oreal Paris and Abaad Organization, a training program that learns how you can safely intervene if you witness or experience street harassment.

projects.title: B5 Fund
projects.description: We referred 216 women-led SMEs to Kafalat and the MFIs Vitas and Al Majmouaa in order to apply for the “Building Beirut Businesses Back and Better – B5 Fund” – That is financed by the Lebanese Financing Facility (LFF), a multi-donor trust fund established Win December 2020, and managed by the World Bank. The Fund aims to support the recovery of targeted micro and small enterprises (MSEs) directly affected by the Port of Beirut blast. Till to date, out of 216 women-led SMEs referred, 36 businesses got cash grants to cover expenses related to working capital, technical services, equipment as well as repairs.

The Fund aims to support the recovery of targeted micro and small enterprises (MSEs) directly affected by the Port of Beirut blast. Till to date, out of 216 women-led SMEs referred, 36 businesses got cash grants to cover expenses related to working capital, technical services, equipment as well as repairs.

On March 8, we launched our joint collaboration, where 8% of the sales was donated to our project in order to support women-owned small businesses, affected by the multiple crises in Lebanon.

projects.title: Al Fanar
projects.description: Stand for Women is proud to have Alfanar Venture Philanthropy as a partner in the Marion Fund. Alfanar is historically a strong supporter of social enterprises. After the devastating Beirut explosion they have dedicated funds to alleviate small businesses & has pooled efforts with Stand For Women to restore some women-owned stores.
body: Stand for Women is proud to have Alfanar Venture Philanthropy as a partner in the Marion Fund. Alfanar is historically a strong supporter of social enterprises. After the devastating Beirut explosion they have dedicated funds to alleviate small businesses & has pooled efforts with Stand For Women to restore some women-owned stores.

In order to repair the core & shell of our joint beneficiaries, Alfanar has contracted BEDCO, which employs youth from Tripoli Beb El Tebbeneh and Jabal Mohsen neighbourhood. These young men are using the professional skills they acquired through March Lebanon Beb El Dahab program and the repairs they executed were awesome & greatly appreciated by the women business owners.

projects.title: Order Of Malta
projects.description: The Order of Malta Lebanon has partnered with Stand for Women, in support of the “Marion Fund” initiative, extending its support to 19 women led SMES: Six months after the Beirut port explosion on the 4th of August. Apart from the help to rebuild and equip their SMEs, women will get coaching, mentoring and training to develop and grow their businesses, in addition to psycho-social support when needed. Thanks to its partners and donors who wholeheartedly responded to their plea right after the explosion.

testimonials.name: Joelle Deaibess
testimonials.text: Volunteering with Stand for Women was a truly enlightening experience of what women’s businesses go through nowadays in our society. It was a true honor seeing how much this NGO cares about helping women stand on their own so they can sustain a business to support them. Women businesses will never suffer again as long as we have people to “stand for women”.

testimonials.name: Christa Maria Daher
testimonials.text: I had an amazing time volunteering with Stand For Women! I was completely immersed in their work and really felt like I was making a difference. The staff was welcoming and informative, and I really enjoyed the diversity of the project. I would highly recommend this organization to anyone looking for an amazing opportunity to make a difference in the world.

testimonials.name: Agness Nohra
testimonials.text: I joined SFW as an intern in December 2022 and this is my last month with them. If I were to describe this journey in a few words, I would put it like this: the magic of being part of a women’s team supporting other women. As simple (and poetic) as this sounds, it was actually one of my best experiences so far. I was assigned to follow up with a woman owner of a one-dollar shop. Besides the procurement of stock and improving the shop’s display, which led to an increase in sales, I got to meet the owner, what made it all special, and listened to her needs. I strongly believe in the power of human connections and that no work would be successful if it’s not based on real connections. I also got to participate in an event where we put a stand for SFW; introduced the organization to participants and sold our merchandise. In addition, I helped with research for some of SFW’s upcoming projects. I focused mainly on the “Young Girls Project” which aims to offer financial help to cover the educational fees of young girls that are dropping out of schools during these hard times. You can see how diverse the projects are and the impact they are making in the community! Not to forget the impacts the whole experience had on me! Last but not least, I got to work with two amazing women, Roula and Sarine, who I admire for their passion, hard work, and the smoothness of creating a friendly working environment.

testimonials.name: Lola Imbert
testimonials.text: I had the opportunity to work alongside SFW. As a French student, I went to Lebanon to join the team and try to help. I was touched by all the encounters in Beirut: the explosion of the port has broken many Lebanese people, but once again, the people show exemplary courage and magnificent mutual aid. Stand for Women has therefore allowed me to be in direct contact with women victims of the explosions; Many of them are fighting for their businesses. Working with Stand for Women was for me many things: meet the women from traveling in the country, support financially the women in their projects, encourage them by running the Beirut Marathon for Women, discover their different talents (cooking, beauty, fashion…) and so on!

testimonials.name: Zoé Kurkowski
testimonials.text: During my stay in Lebanon, I had the opportunity to work with Stand For Women for a short period of time. I was introduced to all the team members that taught me various ideas in a diverse way. Hence my objective was focused on the merchandising projects to launch our products in order to sell them and attract our surrounding to give a wider vision for the NGO. I also was responsible for creating a sales assumption for the new products, however from time to time I had to join small vents held by Stand for Women. I am pleased to have had this wonderful experience and be surrounded by a comfortable and friendly environment. It was a unique experience that allowed me to bring my brick to the building; a real and direct way to help Lebanese women in their professional lives. I am very proud to have been able to work alongside Caroline Fattal and her team, each of them represents a hope for the struggle for women’s rights and the emancipation of women in the Arab world.

testimonials.name: Luana Teychenne
testimonials.text: This internship allowed me to discover the inside and the functioning of an NGO. I loved being in contact with the beneficiaries and talking with them. I had the opportunity to do a lot of tasks like writing the impact report and the newsletter. I was also able to discover the world of communication by taking care of the content of the Twitter page.

testimonials.name: Alexa Chabouté
testimonials.text: I did a 6-months internship in SFW, essentially helping the Project and General Managers through social media communication, fundings seeking and gender advocacy. The team helped me to understand how Lebanese CSO work with their beneficiaries – directly on the field, they explained to me tools they are using and gave me keys to develop my capacity in working abroad. What I liked the most is certainly the fact they followed me since the beginning for me to be in the best environment, since I came in Lebanon alone. They trusted me and gave me some responsibilities. I would have loved to stay longer because a small team involves more time to achieve each project, but it is surely the best way to develop your skills and boost your implication in each task. Thank you!

testimonials.name: Reem Olleik
testimonials.text: My time with Stand For Women was one of the most meaningful and inspiring chapters of my journey. From my very first day working with the team, I was welcomed into an environment full of passion, resilience, and purpose. Contributing to our digital campaigns, advocacy materials, and community events allowed me to bring my own brick to the building for women’s economic empowerment in Lebanon. Working with such fierce, inspiring women gave me both the confidence and the conviction to keep advocating for gender equality and women’s rights wherever I go. Thank you to the entire team for welcoming me so warmly and for empowering me to become the passionate advocate I am today!

testimonials.name: Anissa Bitar
testimonials.text: Holding a Master’s degree in Management from the Lebanese University and a Diploma in Municipal Administration and Finance from the Lebanese American University (LAU), I am a Community Coordinator and Supervisor with over five years of experience working with local and international organizations. I have experience in team supervision, community engagement, stakeholder coordination, and project implementation. I volunteered with Stand for Women, where I supported database management and introduced the organization’s mission to women in the Bekaa and Baalbek regions. This experience enhanced my communication, coordination, and community engagement skills while strengthening my commitment to volunteering and women’s empowerment. I am passionate about humanitarian work and contributing to initiatives that create a positive impact in communities.
